target: thallus (PO_0030027) + surface abaxial (ventral side)
reason: All records are Riccia (Riccia albida, R. albopunctata, R. breutelii). The 'dorsal edge' and 'ventral edge' of a Riccia lobe are the upper and lower outlines of the thallus in cross-section ('flat or slightly convex', 'strongly convex'). So this is the ventral side of the thallus, and the shape is its cross-section outline. 'colorless' probably refers to the ventral scales and should be checked. Bare 'edge' was rejected earlier as generic, but here the flora and genus fix the meaning.

label: thallus air chamber
parent: is_a PO_0025117 (plant anatomical space); part_of PO_0030027 (thallus)
definition: A plant anatomical space (PO:0025117) in the dorsal photosynthetic layer of a thallus (PO:0030027), bounded by walls of chlorophyllose cells and often containing chlorophyllose filaments. It opens to the outside through a thallus air pore, as in the Marchantiales.
reason: A real structure that is diagnostic in Marchantiales (Asterella, Riccia, Plagiochasma): present or absent, in one or several layers, 'irregular', 'spongy', 'with chlorophyllose filaments'. PO has no class for it. It is the companion of the thallus air pore new class proposed on 2026-11-23, and the two should go to PO upstream together.

target: antheridium (PO_0025125) + region apex
reason: In Riccia the antheridia are sunk in the thallus, and only the neck of each antheridial chamber shows on the surface: 'protruding', 'hyaline', 'purplish'. PO has archegonium neck (PO_0030039) but nothing similar for the antheridium. The distal region of the antheridium is the closest expression. A class for the neck of the antheridial chamber could be suggested to PO together with the air chamber, but one flora is not enough to add it.

target: sepal (PO_0009031) at fruit development stage (PO_0001002), pattern 04
reason: The sepals at the fruit stage ('sépales accrescents atteignant 15...'), treated like 'fruit-calyx' and 'fruiting calyx lobe': the bearer is the sepal and the fruit stage is a state of the bearer.

target: lamina (PO_0025060) + region base; leaf lamina base (PO_0008019) when the described organ is the leaf
reason: The base of a blade ('cuneate', 'cordate', 'decurrent'). This is handled like 'lamina margin': in floras it is nearly always the leaf blade, but adding the base region to the lamina of the organ being described also covers bracts and petals.

target: petiolule (PO_0020050)
reason: Exact: a petiolule is by definition the stalk of a leaflet, so 'leaflet' adds nothing. Consistent with 'leaflet stalk' -> petiolule.

target: liverworts: antheridium head (PO_0030075); flowering plants: receptacle (PO_0009064) part of staminate flower (PO_0025600), or hypanthium (PO_0009065) part of staminate flower where the receptacle forms a tube, pattern 12
reason: The records are mixed. In Plagiochasma the male receptacles are the sessile antheridial discs on the dorsal side of the thallus ('dorsal', 'reniform', 'rounded'), which is PO's antheridium head. In Momordica the 'réceptacle cupuliforme' of the male flower is the floral cup, and sex inheres in the flower. The moss/liverwort family rule should separate the two. If the families are not checked, reject the bare word.

target: plant ovary (PO_0009072) + region apex; or plant ovary with the value necked (FLOPO:0991297) when the neck is only mentioned
reason: The narrowed distal part of the ovary below the style ('constricted', 'unconstricted', length, width). Treated like 'hypanthium neck'.

target: container umbel inflorescence (PO_0030129) for the counted part (flower, fruit), pattern 03/14
reason: Not a bearer but the whole in which flowers or legumes are counted ('flowers 2-6', 'legume usually only 1 per umbel'). Same treatment as 'per umbellule' and 'per cymule': the counted part is the subject of the statement.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) part of peduncle (PO_0009053), pattern 12
reason: The hairs of an inflorescence scape (Portuguese 'escapo', 'strap-shaped', 'antrorse'), treated like 'stipule hair'. 'Flowering scape' was mapped to peduncle. Use peduncle rather than stem, which lists scape as a synonym, because these are flowering scapes.

target: corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035)
reason: Exact: the corona lobe class is used for the lobes of the staminal corona (FLOPO_0985022) in Apocynaceae ('columnar', '2.0-2.5 mm high'). Consistent with 'corona segment', 'corona scale' and 'gynostegial corona'.

target: stalk (PO_0025066) part of staminode (PO_0009077), pattern 12
reason: The filament-like stalk of a staminode ('filete linear', 'recurvado no botão'). PO's filament is part of a stamen, which a staminode is not. Same treatment as 'staminode stalk'.

target: leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517)
reason: Narrower: the last-order lobes of a dissected leaf ('ovate', 'linear', 'triangular', 'lanceolate'), the same as 'ultimate lobe'. These are not the liverwort lobule, because the qualities are leaf-segment shapes.

target: tepal (PO_0009033) + position upper (FLOPO_0991376), pattern 18
reason: A positioned part: the tepal on the side towards the axis. The positioned-parts table already treats adaxial petal and sepal as related synonyms of upper petal and sepal. Same treatment as 'dorsal tepal'.

target: secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140)
reason: Narrower: the Cassia, Chamaecrista and Senna treatments count 'pairs of camptodrome (secondaries)', meaning the secondary veins. The venation type is a quality of the secondary vein (eucamptodromous FLOPO_0991303, already used). Counts are pairs (pattern 03).

target: plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of corolla (PO_0009059), bearer_container PO_0009059; petal margin (PO_0025008) when the petals are free
reason: The margin of the corolla or its lobes ('ciliate', 'erose', 'denticulate'), treated like 'fruit margin' and 'ligule margin'.

target: gynostemium (FLOPO_0986015)
reason: Exact: a spelling variant (Turkish 'Ginostemiyum 0,4 × 0,5 cm') of gynostemium, the orchid column.

target: shoot system (PO_0009006) with the quality young (PATO_0000309), pattern 04, only when preceded by 'young' or 'new'
reason: In floras 'growth' with indumentum and 'zig-zag' is the young shoots ('young growth minutely puberulent'). Same treatment as 'young growth'. Without 'young' or 'new' in the sentence the bare word is too vague and should not be grounded.

target: awn (PO_0025349) + position lateral (FLOPO_0991380), pattern 18
reason: A positioned part: the side awns of a three-awned lemma (for example Aristida), which can be absent or present, exserted or included. The 'lateral' context word does not list 'awn' yet, and it should be added.

target: vascular leaf (PO_0009025) + position axillary (FLOPO:0991000), pattern 18
reason: The axillary leaf of Selaginella, the single leaf at each branch fork ('micrófilo axilar ovado', 'base arredondada'). PO's microphyll (PO_0020053) is obsolete, so its leaves fall under vascular leaf. An existing position expresses 'axillary', so no new class is needed.

Ambiguous without context. It could be the mouth of a corolla, calyx, pitcher, perianth tube or fruit, and 'vertical', 'oblique' and 'blunt' do not settle which. The organ-named forms ('pitcher mouth', 'corolla orifice') are handled separately.

target: container capsule fruit (PO_0030091) for the counted seeds, pattern 03/14
reason: The whole in which seeds are counted ('seeds usually 1 per capsule', '6-10-seeded'). Same treatment as 'per umbellule' and 'per dichasium'. The counted part is seed, which the 'seeded' suffix rule already gives.

target: pinna (FLOPO_0985027), count with count_position each_side, landmark leaf rachis (PO_0020055); pattern 14
reason: A count at a position: 'pinnae 61-71 per side' of the rachis, the same as 'lateral veins per side'. The counted part is named, so this is not the bare fragment 'per side of rachi'.

target: higher order inflorescence axis (PO_0009081)
reason: Narrower: Spanish 'raquila' and Latinised 'rachiola' are the flower-bearing branches of a palm (or other branched) inflorescence ('raquilas ca. 15-36', 'tomentose'). Same treatment as 'rachillae'. This is not the grass spikelet rachilla (PO_0009080).

target: non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075) part of gametophore stem (PO_0030022), on its stipe (the unbranched basal portion), pattern 12
reason: The records are mosses (Mittenothamnium, Micralsopsis, Pinnatella), where stipitate or frondose stems have differentiated leaves on the bare lower stipe ('small', 'clasping', 'squarrose', 'differentiated'). This contrasts with branch leaves. Stem leaves of mosses were treated the same way. 'stipe leaf margin', 'stipe leaf cell' and 'stipe leaf costa' then follow from the region and part patterns.

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656) part of anther (PO_0009066), pattern 12
reason: The apical gland of the anther or connective (Acmadenia, Dinizia, Kalanchoe: 'apical', 'conspicuous', 'red-brown'). Treated like 'calyx gland' and 'receptacle gland'.

target: calyx (PO_0009060) part of fruit (PO_0009001) at fruit development stage (PO_0001002); its distance below the fruit apex through pattern 09
reason: In Lecythidaceae pyxidia (Allantoma, Cariniana, Couratari) the calycine ring is the persistent rim of the calyx on the fruit wall ('a continuous rim 3 mm wide', 'ridged', '1.5 cm below apex'). It is the remains of the calyx at the fruit stage, as with 'fruit-calyx'. 'Below apex' is a position relative to another part. The ring is used in one family only, so a new class is not justified.

target: Annonaceae: monocarp (FLOPO_0986046); Malvaceae: mericarp (PO_0020075)
reason: Narrower: Portuguese 'carpídio' is the fruitlet from one carpel. In Annonaceae (Xylopia, Cardiopetalum) it is the monocarp of the apocarpous fruit; in Malvaceae (Abutilon, Bakeridesia) it is a mericarp of the schizocarp. 'Carpodium absent' probably means abortive fruitlets. The family has to decide the target.

target: connective (PO_0009068) + region apex; connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073) when the connective is prolonged beyond the thecae
reason: The tip of the anther connective ('truncado', 'agudo', 'apiculate'). When it is prolonged into a structure with its own length, it is the connective appendage.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) part of fruit (PO_0009001), with position median (FLOPO_0991381)
reason: The central vein of a flattened fruit or fruit valve ('nervadura-central no saliente', 'slightly raised'). Treated like 'glume midrib'. Low confidence because the records may describe the midrib of a fruit wing (samara) or of a persistent bract rather than the fruit body.
